cards.prompt: According to Robert Greene's Mastery, what are the two kinds of failure?
cards.answer: One from never trying out ideas due to fear or waiting for perfect time (cannot learn from it), and one from bold trying (greatly outweighed by learning).

cards.prompt: Rereading a text for hours is a reliable way to build durable memory.
cards.answer: Myth: rereading is time consuming, gives non-durable memory, and familiarity feels like mastery.

cards.prompt: Learning that is easy is like writing in ____: here today and gone tomorrow.
Cal Newport's two core abilities for the new economy are mastering hard things quickly and...
options: producing at an elite level in quality and speed
cards.answer: Producing at an elite level, in both quality and speed.

cards.prompt: You are about to read a new math chapter. Per Make It Stick, what should you do before reading the solution, even if you may get it wrong?
cards.answer: Try to solve the problem first; attempting before being taught leads to better learning even with errors.

cards.prompt: Explain like I'm 10: why do jobs often feel easier to enjoy than free time?
cards.answer: Jobs come with goals, feedback and challenges that pull you in. Free time has no structure, so you must shape it into something fun yourself.

cards.prompt: Mastery can be earned only one way. Which option is that way, unlike the other three that cannot get you mastery?
cards.answer: Mastery can only be earned through hard work; money, impatience and privilege cannot give it.
